meta.role: You are two readers at once. First, a line editor holding the text to Strunk and White's "The Elements of Style" — the rules are concrete and you score against them. Second, Robert Gottlieb at the editor's desk — voice, momentum, economy, and whether the piece earns the reader's attention; this is judgment, not a checklist. You are not a fan. You are looking for where the prose is flabby, where the blend collapses into formula, and where it stops sounding like a person.

audit_request.mission: Generate 10 fresh triadic-voice paragraphs (Russell rigor x Feynman intuition x Hoskinson momentum) on 10 different topics, then grade them as prose against two standards — The Elements of Style and Gottlieb's editorial sensibility — and analyze how the three-voice blend holds (or fails) across the set. The point of 10 paragraphs is to expose what one or two cannot: formulaic openings, a recurring analogy crutch, one voice quietly taking over, the discipline floor slipping when the topic gets dry. Produce audit.md and corrections.json.

context.what_to_read: - `tools/build-voice-corpus/scripts/generate.py` — the generator. Read `build_generation_prompt` and the `triadic` branch; you will replicate that exact corpus-grounded prompt so the audit reflects what the real system produces. - `skills/russellian-style/assets/hoskinson-corpus/index.json` — 57 real exemplars (his own transcribed words) with `rhetorical_move` + `tags`. This is the Hoskinson grounding. - `skills/russellian-style/assets/hoskinson-corpus/transcripts/*.md` — full transcripts, to internalize his actual cadence and tics ("always warm always sunny sometimes colorado", "the thing people miss", systems-tradeoff framing, walk-before-you-run, candor). - `skills/russellian-style/references/triadic-voice-guide.md` — the fusion contract: open Hoskinson, develop Feynman, close Russell; discipline floor still applies. - `skills/russellian-style/assets/feynman-corpus/index.json` — pointers only; draw Feynman's contribution from the guide, never quote verbatim Feynman text.
context.discipline_floor: The russellian-style linters are the quality floor the prose must clear regardless of voice: no hedging, active voice, signal density (restraint on adjectives/adverbs), parallel structure, sentence-rhythm variance. Score these too; do not let "warmth" excuse a hedge or a passive.

generation_protocol.step: Read `generate.py::build_generation_prompt`. For each topic below, assemble the SAME triadic prompt it builds: a deterministic selection of Hoskinson exemplars (vary the seed per topic so the exemplar set is not identical across all 10 — use seed = topic index 1..10), plus the full triadic-voice guide, plus the open-Hoskinson / develop-Feynman / close-Russell instruction.

Write one paragraph (150-220 words) per topic, in the triadic fusion voice, grounded in the exemplars. The 10 topics (use all, in order): 1. Why a zero-knowledge proof lets you verify a computation without learning its inputs. 2. Why formal verification belongs at the base layer of a blockchain. 3. Why proof-of-stake decentralizes better than proof-of-work. 4. What "finality" means in a proof-of-stake system, and why it is hard. 5. Why on-chain governance has to earn legitimacy rather than assume it. 6. Why a self-funding treasury changes the incentives of a protocol. 7. Why self-sovereign identity (DIDs) reorganizes trust online. 8. Why cross-chain interoperability is harder than scaling a single chain. 9. Why peer review and academic rigor belong inside engineering, not beside it. 10. What a financial operating system for a billion people actually has to get right. Also write 2 PURE-Hoskinson control paragraphs (topics 2 and 9) so you can measure how much the fusion changes the voice versus pure Hoskinson. All passages must clear the discipline floor. Do not reuse the same opening move or the same analogy across paragraphs; if you catch yourself doing it, that is itself a finding to report.

rubric_elements_of_style.note: Strunk and White. Score each paragraph 0-5 per rule; 5 = exemplary, 0 = violated throughout. Cite the offending words.
rubric_elements_of_style.rule: Vigorous writing is concise. Every word tells. Flag filler, redundant pairs, throat-clearing.
Prefer the active voice. Flag every passive and judge whether it is load-bearing or lazy.
Prefer the specific to the general, the concrete to the abstract. Flag vague abstractions ("solutions", "ecosystem", "leverage").
Put statements in positive form. Flag "not un-", "did not have much confidence in", hedged negatives.
Express coordinate ideas in parallel form. Flag broken parallelism in lists and pairs.
Keep related words together; misplaced modifiers and split logic cost clarity.
Avoid "rather, very, little, pretty" and other leeches; flag intensifier inflation.
A paragraph is a unit of thought; flag drift across more than one.
Do not overstate; flag hype the reader will discount ("revolutionary", "the greatest", "everyone knows").
Prefer the standard to the offbeat; flag cleverness that draws attention to itself.

rubric_gottlieb.note: Robert Gottlieb's editorial sensibility — judgment, not a checklist. Score each paragraph 0-5 per dimension and explain the call in one sentence.
rubric_gottlieb.dimension: Does it sound like a specific person with these three influences, or like generic competent prose? The editor's first job is to protect the voice.
Does each sentence pull you to the next, or does the piece stall? Pace is a real property; flat stretches are a defect.
Does every sentence earn its place? Gottlieb cut for the reader. Mark what you would cut and why.
Is the idea delivered cleanly on first read, or does the reader have to reread? Cleverness that obscures is a failure.
Does the paragraph have an arc — a setup, a turn, a landing — or is it a flat list? The triadic contract (open/develop/close) should produce shape; check that it does.
Does it over-explain, restate, or condescend? Good editing removes the sentence that tells the reader what the previous sentence already showed.
At 150-220 words, is the length justified, or is it padded to hit a target? Would it be better at 120?

blend_analysis.note: The heart of this iteration. Per paragraph and across the set.
blend_analysis.per_paragraph: Identify the Hoskinson, Feynman, and Russell contributions explicitly (quote the spans). Score each voice's presence 0-5. State: is it balanced (each >= 3, spread <= 2), or does one dominate and one vanish? Is the open/develop/close sequencing actually present, or stapled?
blend_analysis.across_the_set: This is what 10 paragraphs reveal that 1 cannot: - Formula detection: do paragraphs reuse the same opening gambit, the same "imagine you and I" analogy frame, the same closing "reduces to one sentence" move? Quote the repeats. A blend that only works one way is a template, not a voice. - Voice drift: does Feynman thin out on the abstract topics (governance, legitimacy) and Hoskinson take over? Does Russell collapse into the same final aphorism every time? - Topic sensitivity: which topics did the blend serve well, which did it fight? A real voice adapts; a brittle one sounds the same regardless of subject. - Compare the 2 pure-Hoskinson controls to their triadic versions: did the fusion add Feynman intuition and Russell compression, or just decorate?

deliverables.deliverable: Sections in order: 1. Verdict (one paragraph): overall prose grade (A-F) and whether the blend is a genuine adaptive voice or a working-but-formulaic template. Be decisive. 2. The 10 paragraphs + 2 controls, verbatim. 3. Per-paragraph scorecards: a compact table with the Elements-of-Style rule scores, the Gottlieb dimension scores, the three voice-presence scores, and a one-line editor's note. 4. Cross-set blend analysis (formula detection with quoted repeats, voice drift, topic sensitivity, control comparison). 5. Discipline-floor results (hedge/passive/density flags; note false positives on his tics). 6. Prioritized fixes — concrete edits to `generate.py`'s triadic prompt or to `triadic-voice-guide.md` that would raise the prose grade or break the formula (e.g. a "vary the opening" instruction, a ban on the reused analogy, a Russell-close that is not always an aphorism). House style for your own prose: no "key insight", no rule-of-three padding, no em-dash overuse.

constraints.copyright: Never quote verbatim Feynman text; his contribution is drawn from the guide. Hoskinson exemplars are his own content. Do not store or reproduce anything beyond what the corpus already contains.
constraints.honesty: Cite specific words for every score below 4 and every claim of formula. Do not hand-wave. A short, evidence-backed audit beats a long one. If you cannot run the linters, score the discipline floor by hand and say so.
constraints.standards: The Elements of Style is a rulebook — score mechanically. Gottlieb is judgment — explain each call. Keep them separate; do not average them into one mush.

audit_request.output_format: Produce the two files as separate fenced blocks: audit.md (markdown) first, then corrections.json (valid JSON against the schema). No commentary outside the two files.
